title: The critical activation density in graph bootstrap percolation
summary: In graph bootstrap percolation, edges of an Erdős-Rényi random graph ${\mathcal G}_{n,p}$ are initially active, and activation spreads to other edges of $K_n$ via the combinatorics of a fixed graph $H$: an edge becomes active whenever it is the unique inactive edge in a copy of $H$. The process $H$-percolates if all edges of $K_n$ are eventually activated. While classical cases such as $H=K_3$ (connectivity) and $H=K_4$ (related to $2$-neighbor bootstrap percolation) have been studied extensively, general graphs $H$ can exhibit wildly different behaviors.
